newsitem.title: JAPAN: Youths nab Nikes in Japan's first sneaker robbery.
newsitem.headline: Youths nab Nikes in Japan's first sneaker robbery.

text.p: A Japanese teenage gang on Tuesday beat up three men and stole a pair of coveted Air Max brand sneakers from one of them, police said.
A police spokesman said it was the nation's first known case of robbery of the shoes, made by NIKE Inc, which are the subject of a major fashion craze in Japan.

Used pairs of the prized U.S.-made sneakers, which have compartments built into the heel and sole visible through transparent plastic bubbles, fetch up to $1,000 in shops where trend-crazy youths snap them up as quickly as they appear.
The robbery in the early hours of Tuesday took place in a park in the city of Sakai, near the western commercial centre of Osaka, police said.
After a brawl started, the five teenagers grabbed steel pipes from a car they had been riding in and attacked the men, causing slight facial cuts to all three.
They then made off with cash and the pair of sneakers.
In a fad which took off last year, Japanese youths bid against each other in shops when Nike sneakers are available.
